title: Beef Stroganoff
subtitle: Tender strips of beef in a paprika and soured cream sauce
excerpt: Thin strips of sirloin or fillet quickly fried with mushrooms, onion, and paprika, finished with a generous spoonful of soured cream. A Russian classic that became a British mid-century favourite.

recipe.sourceNotes: Beef stroganoff is named after the Stroganov family, prominent Russian aristocrats in the 19th century. The original recipe was a simple dish of sautéed beef strips in a sauce of mustard and bouillon. The addition of mushrooms and soured cream evolved over time, and the dish spread internationally following the Russian diaspora after the Revolution. It became extremely popular in Britain, France, and America in the 1950s and 60s as an easily adaptable recipe for home cooks. The key technical point is that the beef must be fried very quickly at high heat to stay tender: it is a last-minute dish and should not be left to braise in the sauce.

content.text: High heat is essential for the beef: it must fry, not steam. This means frying in small batches so the pan does not become crowded. A crowded pan lowers the temperature and the beef will stew rather than colour. The soured cream should be stirred in at the very end with the heat off, then the pan returned to low heat just long enough to warm through: boiling the cream will cause it to split.

items.preparation: cut into thin strips against the grain

content.text: Season the beef strips with salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a wide, heavy pan over very high heat. Fry the beef in two batches for 1 to 2 minutes per batch until browned. Remove and set aside.

Reduce the heat to medium. Add the butter and fry the onion for 5 minutes until softened. Add the garlic and mushrooms. Fry for 5 minutes until the mushrooms have coloured and the liquid has evaporated. Add the paprika and cook for 30 seconds.

Return the beef to the pan. Stir in the mustard and Worcestershire sauce. Remove from the heat. Stir in the soured cream until combined. Return to the lowest heat and warm through for 1 minute without boiling. Taste for seasoning. Scatter with parsley and serve immediately with rice or egg noodles.
